races.name: Killik Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sky Secret
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Clive Cox and Rossa Ryan, winning at this course and distance on good ground; has the early pace to see off Arabica Queen for the lead, and five-from-five on similar going underlines how well she handles these conditions, but will face pressure from the first stride.|
runners_data.comment: Sky Secret showed a win four starts back and returns on a sharp 11-day turnaround carrying 136 lb from stall 4, with experience over today's trip and a rating of 91 suggesting he holds strong claims — the risk is that he has been out of the frame in his last three starts.

runners_data.name: Innichen
runners_data.note: William Buick takes over on this hold-up type who has been in excellent form, winning twice and placing twice in five similar-ground starts; drops to five furlongs where a strong pace will play to her closing style, though she must find daylight in a compressed finish.|
runners_data.comment: Innichen showed his class when winning two of his last six starts, with a third two outings back keeping him in good heart before an unplaced effort last time; he has experience over today's trip and going, and 135 lb from stall two makes him one to respect here.

runners_data.name: Undercover Affair
runners_data.note: David Evans's prominent racer has a strong record on good ground at five furlongs and returns after a 21-day break in good form under Billy Loughnane; ideally positioned to track the front-running duel and has the fitness and course experience to capitalise in the closing stages.|
runners_data.comment: Undercover Affair arrives here on the back of a win three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and conditions is a clear asset carrying 131 lb from stall five; the risk is that his last two outings have yielded only a fifth and an eighth.

runners_data.name: Betty Boop
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on this hold-up filly who won over six furlongs on good ground and drops back to five for Richard Hughes; her last three runs are limited but encouraging, and a contested pace is exactly what she needs to deploy her finishing kick — the trip is the only query.|
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back and third three starts back, Betty Boop arrives in decent nick on 20 days' rest, has run over today's trip, and our rating of 83 supports her claims; the fifth last time out is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Rotelle
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes's two-year-old carries a hood and has already won over five furlongs on good ground, placing twice in three similar-going starts; prominent in style, Paddy Bradley will look to sit just off the pace duo and her consistent record at the trip makes her well-suited to this scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Rotelle ran well to finish second last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, but that eighth two starts back is a blot, and carrying 128 lb from stall three while ranked fifth of eight on ratings suggests he faces a stiff task here.

runners_data.name: Arabica Queen
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's front-runner has a win over six furlongs and steps back to five under Jason Watson; she has placed in four of five similar-going starts but faces an early fight with Sky Secret for the lead — if she fails to dominate, she may find the trip too sharp having burned energy contesting the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Arabica Queen comes into this off a 28-day break with experience over today's trip, and a win three starts back shows she can find the winner's enclosure, though she was unplaced last time and ranks sixth of eight on our ratings, so she faces a stiff task from stall one carrying 123 lb.

runners_data.name: Holi Scarlett
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's filly has been consistently placed without winning from a prominent position, going one-from-seven on similar going; Sean Levey will aim to sit handy, and while she handles these conditions well, her inability to clinch races when competitive is a concern in a competitive nursery.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Holi Scarlett faces a stiff ask, though she does offer some encouragement — third last time out, and a winner four starts back, with experience over today's trip and going and a 27-day break suggesting she returns fresh.

runners_data.name: True Charm
runners_data.note: Lemos De Souza's filly is a genuine prominent-racing type by nature but is mapped to midfield here because more prominent horses than can naturally slot in ahead of her; returning after 49 days off with only one placing in three starts, her chance is further tempered by racing out of her preferred position in this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, True Charm faces a stiff ask here; a return to today's going and a second three starts back offer slim encouragement, but 49 days off the track adds another question mark.

races.paceDynamic: Sky Secret and Arabica Queen are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead from the gates, creating a genuinely contested pace over Sandown's straight five furlongs on good ground. Sky Secret, trained by Clive Cox and ridden by Rossa Ryan, has led or raced prominently in all recent starts and will not easily concede that berth; Arabica Queen, down in trip from her recent successes at six furlongs, will be keen to establish herself early under Jason Watson. The resulting honest-to-strong gallop is likely to compress the field quickly, with Undercover Affair, Rotelle, and Holi Scarlett pushing into prominent positions, while Innichen and Betty Boop, genuine hold-up types, will be held back for a late run. This race shape — two front-runners fighting for supremacy over a flat, straight five — classically favours prominent-to-midfield horses who can sit just off the contested pace and pounce in the final furlong, making Undercover Affair, Rotelle, and a closing Innichen the profiles to focus on. The field holds more prominent types than can all occupy that position; Sky Secret has the pace edge to lead outright, with Arabica Queen most likely to slot into a close-up second early, and True Charm — a genuine prominent type — is mapped to midfield and unlikely to secure that position in this shape, discounting its chance accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Sky Secret and Arabica Queen fight for the lead and set an honest gallop that strings the field out, setting up the race for those tracking just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Undercover Affair and Rotelle, positioned just behind the duel, travel into the race with minimal effort and have the energy to quicken in the final furlong as the front two tire; good-ground form at the trip suits both, and their jockeys — Loughnane and Bradley — have the tactical awareness to exploit a pacemaker's collapse.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running duel between Sky Secret and Arabica Queen is fierce enough to burn them both off, leaving a late gap for Innichen and Betty Boop.
scenarios.body: Innichen, with William Buick aboard, has strong recent form over this trip and going and is adept at finishing hard; Betty Boop under Oisin Murphy has shown a classy turn of foot at shorter distances and will relish the strong pace pulling her into contention.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Sky Secret successfully sees off Arabica Queen in the opening two furlongs and establishes a comfortable, controlled lead from which she can dictate tempo.
scenarios.body: Clive Cox's filly showed a course-and-distance win in recent form and handles good ground perfectly; if the pace is not truly fast enough to stop her, Rossa Ryan can balance her up and kick again inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Pace, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is uneven or collapses mid-race, creating a muddling tempo that compresses the field and invites a wider spread of finishers.
scenarios.body: Holi Scarlett, consistent without winning from a prominent position, could benefit from a falsely-run race where positional advantage rather than raw speed determines the winner; True Charm, though racing out of its natural role having been pushed back to midfield, would need this scenario to be competitive at all.

watchPoints.text: Watch Sky Secret and Arabica Queen in the first furlong — if both are hard ridden for the lead by their jockeys, the early fractions will be blistering and will likely end the chance of either winning.|

Innichen carries fitness concerns having run eight days ago, but William Buick's hold-up ride means she needs a clear run in a field of eight — any traffic issues in the final furlong from stall position could cost her.|
True Charm's 49-day absence combined with being forced to race behind its natural position makes it vulnerable to being outpaced early and unable to recover; monitor in-running if it settles poorly.|

Betty Boop has only three career runs and drops in trip; watch whether Oisin Murphy settles her in the early stages or if she races too keenly off a contested pace, which could undermine her late finishing effort.|

Rotelle's headgear (hood) is worth monitoring at the start — if it helps her focus and she breaks cleanly, Paddy Bradley can slot her ideally between the front-running pair and the hold-up horses in the perfect prominent position.|

races.name: Killik Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: South Shore
runners_data.note: Most progressive horse in the field on form (1-1-2-2-2 run), William Carson's stable partner for Robert Cowell who has posted 10 top-three finishes from 15 starts on similar going; a genuine hold-up type who needs the pace to lift to pounce, and four days between runs is sharp enough.|
runners_data.comment: South Shore has been a model of consistency, placed in each of his last six starts with wins four and five starts back, and he has raced over today's distance and going before; the concern is whether four days is enough recovery time carrying 138 lb.

runners_data.name: Good Earth
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up performer with 15 starts on comparable going and a placed effort at this course and trip; Connor Planas takes the mount for a yard that has been in solid recent form (4 from 15 in 14 days), though a run of 6-5-18-2-4 suggests inconsistency at the top of the market.|
runners_data.comment: Good Earth is our top-rated runner and arrives fresh on 15 days' rest, carrying 138 lb from stall 7, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour. Winless in his last six starts, but a second four starts back hints at better, and an rating of 80 makes him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Duskaura
runners_data.note: Three-year-old course-and-distance winner who finished 1st over 6f on Good 21 days ago; a natural hold-up operator on the Tony Carroll team, which is 3 from 36 in 14 days, but 9 placed efforts from 12 on similar going underlines she handles conditions — likely needs six furlongs to be at her best.|
runners_data.comment: Duskaura arrives here on the back of a win two starts ago and has experience of today's trip and going, with a rating of 77 suggesting she holds strong claims against this field; the risk is that eighth last time out leaves a question mark over her current form.

runners_data.name: Hint Of Humour
runners_data.note: Prominent-style four-year-old with a strong placed record (five places from last five starts), and Rossa Ryan is an upgrade in class; 66 days off the track is the concern, but on Good going over this distance at Sandown the profile fits neatly behind an uncontested pace.|
runners_data.comment: Hint Of Humour returns third last time out and has placed second on three occasions in recent starts, giving her a strong profile as a danger here, though a 66-day absence and a winless run in her last six starts are the risks to weigh.

runners_data.name: Maharajas Express
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane takes the ride on a six-year-old with two wins on Good ground from 15 similar-going starts; at his core a true hold-up horse, though the crowded rear means he is mapped to midfield and is likely to race out of his most effective position, which tempers expectations significantly.|
runners_data.comment: Maharajas Express won two starts back but has otherwise struggled in recent starts, finishing sixth or worse on four occasions in that spell; he has run over today's trip and going, and 135 lb is no easy ask, though an 11-day turnaround suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Level Up
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner for David Evans, with Oisin Murphy a significant booking; headgear (blinkers) applied, and a record of 1W-5P from seven Good-ground starts shows he travels well at this pace — ran 2nd four times from the front before winning, underlining he handles being caught and is hard to pass.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back but has since slipped to sixth, and while he has run over today's trip and going, the 135 lb burden from stall nine may test his ability to recapture that form against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Cameley Days
runners_data.note: Prominent four-year-old fitted with blinkers for Chris Dwyer's yard (1 from 8 in 14 days); Lewis Edmunds rides and the horse has placed five times in nine Good-ground starts, with a win over 5f on Good last year — suited by sitting just off the pace and likely to give Level Up a race in the straight.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Cameley Days has struggled for consistency in recent starts, with just one win in her last six and back-to-back disappointing efforts latest; a third three starts back offers little encouragement, though she has distance and going experience and returns fit on 14 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Jenny Jerome
runners_data.note: Three-year-old by a trainer with no wins from five in 14 days and 125 days off the track — the significant absence is a red flag; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural style is negated by the race shape, and limited form on Good ground (3 from 7) makes her a speculative outsider even if everything clicks.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Jenny Jerome faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and did finish second two starts back — a small crumb of comfort after 125 days off the track.

runners_data.name: So Smart
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old regular equipped with a hood and tongue tie for Grace Harris (5 from 15 in 14 days, showing good yard form); Laura Coughlan claims 3lb, and So Smart has won and placed multiple times on Good ground over five furlongs — but as a genuine closer parked in midfield, the race shape works against her natural strengths.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures and his recent form has been patchy, with a seventh last time out clouding an earlier win three starts back; he has run over today's trip and going, and stall one is a neutral fact, but 130 lb makes the task no easier.

races.paceDynamic: Level Up is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival pressing from the outside, Oisin Murphy can dictate terms unchallenged through the first two furlongs before the field strings out on Sandown's straight five. Hint Of Humour and Cameley Days will push forward to prominent positions just off the leader, creating an organised, measured gallop rather than a contested burn — the kind of tempo that often suits the horse controlling it. The field holds more hold-up types than can genuinely settle at the rear: Maharajas Express, Jenny Jerome and So Smart are true closers redistributed into midfield slots on the map, meaning the back of the field is less populated with genuine late-kickers than it appears. This race shape most strongly favours front-running and prominent horses who can travel within themselves and use their early position rather than closers who depend on a strong pace to reel in a relaxed leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Level Up Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Murphy slots Level Up into an uncontested lead and the pace remains measured throughout.
scenarios.body: Level Up has won and placed repeatedly off the front on Good ground over this exact course and distance, and with no rival able to match its early stride, it can dictate every fraction and simply quicken clear entering the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Swallow Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Cameley Days or Hint Of Humour track Level Up tightly and overhaul it in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: A modest, controlled pace suits the two prominent raiders who sit within a length of the leader, conserving energy to challenge when Level Up finally ties up; Hint Of Humour's consistent placed record at this trip on Good gives it the strongest claim.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Sprint Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and midfield horses get a genuine tow into the race.
scenarios.body: South Shore and Good Earth have both won or placed off a strong tempo on Good ground over five furlongs and carry the best recent form to benefit from a contested finish; Duskaura, a course-and-distance winner, could also arrive late if the pace lifts.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Hold-Ups Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the true hold-up horses find enough daylight from their unnatural mid-pack berths to finish through.
scenarios.body: Maharajas Express, Jenny Jerome and So Smart are genuine closers shunted into midfield on the map, meaning they must race out of role in a race where the pace is unlikely to be generous enough to generate the gaps they need; only a surprisingly fast-run race would give them a realistic passage.

watchPoints.text: Level Up — if Murphy travels untouched in front past halfway, the race is likely already won; watch for whether any prominent horse has the early pace to match strides and apply genuine pressure before the furlong pole.

Hint Of Humour — 66 days off the track is the critical unknown; if Ryan has it tuned up it is the likeliest to overhaul the leader, but a flat run after the break would confirm the layoff has taken its toll.

Maharajas Express and So Smart — both genuine closers forced to race from midfield in a race with a controlled pace; if they are seen tracking Level Up too closely early it signals they have compromised their style, and their chances dim accordingly.

South Shore — sharp four-day turnaround for Robert Cowell's consistent hold-up performer; watch where Ghiani positions it in the first furlong — if the pace is modest and he finds himself too far back with nowhere to sprint through, its fine recent form counts for little.

Cameley Days — the blinkers application and proximity to Level Up makes it a notable each-way factor; if Lewis Edmunds can settle it in second without burning too much petrol, it has the profile to be the main danger to the favourite in the final 100 yards.

races.name: House Of Killik Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hungarian
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win last time out at Sandown over 7f on Standard; stepping up to a mile here which could suit his profile, though trainer Lemos De Souza has a modest 1/11 in the last 14 days and the tongue-tie is a minor flag to watch.
runners_data.comment: Hungarian arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, giving him a solid profile heading in; carrying 137 lb from stall five is the one query, but at a rating of 92 he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Home Hero
runners_data.note: Two-day turnaround is the standout concern — Hugo Palmer has him back quickly after a win on good ground and while he's proven over this trip and going (2W from 8 Good runs), front-runners who have raced very recently can fade when the gallop gets honest.
runners_data.comment: Home Hero won two starts back but was well beaten last time out, and at just two days since his last run, freshness must be a question mark; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 135 lb from stall seven, and faces a competitive field ranked fifth of eight.

runners_data.name: Magic Trip
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning from a 77-day break for Andrew Balding, who is in form (11/66 T14); the layoff could mean a freshness advantage or ring-rustiness, and his form at two miles-plus distances suggests the mile trip may genuinely suit better than his recent longer outings.
runners_data.comment: Magic Trip arrives with distance and going experience to call on and catches the eye on a rating of 81, yet he is winless in his last five starts and that fifth-placed effort last time out after a 77-day absence leaves improvement needed to land this.

runners_data.name: Thursday Girl
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent front-runner for Ed Walker — four seconds and a win from five recent starts on good ground, with Oisin Murphy booked, and her natural jumping style means she won't be stopping to fight for the lead; the key question is whether battling Home Hero tests her beyond her comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Thursday Girl returns in fair heart after winning two starts back, though her recent record shows four runner-up finishes in her last five, suggesting she finds one too good; she has experience over today's trip and going, but the 132 lb is a stiff ask from stall six.

runners_data.name: Drymee
runners_data.note: Progressive hold-up horse who has won twice over a mile on good ground recently; Billy Loughnane gives him a strong closing-style partnership, and a genuine pace duel up front is the scenario that brings his finishing kick into play most effectively.
runners_data.comment: Drymee won back-to-back two and three starts back, has form over today's trip and going, and steps into the plate fresh enough at 20 days since his third last time out; the weight burden of 132 lb from stall four is the one factor to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Dovecote
runners_data.note: Lightly raced by Ralph Beckett with just three runs and two placed efforts; the small sample makes form reading difficult but both places came at a mile on varying ground, and Rossa Ryan is a shrewd judge of pace for a prominent type looking to sit close and pounce.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with two runner-up finishes doing little to disguise a modest speed rating of 63, Dovecote faces a stiff task from stall eight carrying 131 lb, though he has run over today's trip and returns on a reasonable 36-day break.

runners_data.name: Tamzan
runners_data.note: In-form horse with two recent wins at a mile on good ground, but its genuine hold-up style means it has been mapped to midfield here due to field congestion — the race shape may not naturally deliver the position it needs, and the 0/11 trainer strike rate in the last 14 days adds a minor negative layer.
runners_data.comment: Tamzan won last time out and was third two starts back, but she ranks last on our figures in a field of eight and that gulf makes her very difficult to fancy despite the experience over today's trip and going and a timely 19-day break.

runners_data.name: Glen Nevis
runners_data.note: All six career runs on good ground, ideal conditions for William Buick to deploy his tactical intelligence from a prominent position; has been placed three times without winning, and while the handicapper may have him right, Buick's course knowledge and the likely strong pace make this a live each-way profile.
runners_data.comment: Glen Nevis shaped with plenty of promise when second last time out and has experience over today's trip and going, with our rating of 81 marking him out as a leading threat; the risk is that he has been winless in his last six starts, and that elusive win remains to be delivered.

races.paceDynamic: Home Hero and Thursday Girl are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the break over Sandown's one-mile trip, creating a genuinely contested pace rather than a dawdle. With two horses fighting for the same real estate from the outset, the gallop should be honest and sustained — neither can afford to concede ground early, which will stretch the field and minimise any chance of a tactical crawl. The prominent types — Hungarian, Dovecote, and Glen Nevis — will look to sit just off the battle and pounce, while Drymee and Magic Trip will be further back hoping the pace burns out the leaders. This race shape favours hold-up and late-finishing profiles in theory, but the redistribution note is critical: Tamzan is a true hold-up horse pushed into midfield on the map because the field carries more closers than the rear can accommodate, meaning its chance is tempered by running out of its natural role. On balance, the contested pace and honest gallop most rewards prominent trackers who can sit within striking distance of the leaders without burning their petrol — horses who can travel economically just off the duel and pounce inside the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Suits Trackers
scenarios.trigger: If Home Hero and Thursday Girl fight it out up front, burning each other off and leaving the well-placed prominent horses to swoop.
scenarios.body: The early battle between the two front-runners will likely drain their reserves in the final furlong, opening the door for horses who travel just off the pace — Hungarian and Dovecote have both shown the ability to sit handy and quicken, with Thursday Girl's consistent placed record suggesting she may simply outstay Home Hero if she can manage the duel. Glen Nevis, ridden by Buick and proven on good ground at this trip, is the natural tracker to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fierce enough to genuinely compromise both leaders, a true hold-up horse gets a clear run and picks up the pieces late.
scenarios.body: Drymee has won twice over a mile on good ground recently and Billy Loughnane is an aggressive closer's jockey who knows how to time a late run; a strong pace makes this scenario genuinely viable. Magic Trip showed a placed effort at a mile on similar ground and, with a 77-day break potentially meaning a fresher horse, could outfinish a tired field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: One Pacer Leads Cheaply
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners backs off early — particularly Home Hero, who is only 2 days off his last run and could be managed more conservatively — Thursday Girl leads at a comfortable tempo.
scenarios.body: A calmer early fractions would play into Thursday Girl's hands given her remarkable placed record (four seconds and a win from five recent starts), allowing her to control the pace and kick clear with Oisin Murphy executing a front-running masterclass. Hungarian and Glen Nevis would be closest pursuers but face a harder task overhauling an undisturbed leader running on good ground she handles well.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail to Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves less fierce than expected and mid-to-rear horses are left with too much to do off a slow tempo.
scenarios.body: Hold-up runners like Magic Trip and Tamzan — with Tamzan already racing out of its natural position — find themselves with insufficient gallop to build momentum from behind, leaving them flat-footed in the straight. Dovecote and Glen Nevis, tracking closely throughout, emerge as the main beneficiaries alongside the lead pair.

watchPoints.text: Home Hero runs just 2 days after his last start — watch for signs in the paddock and early strides that the quick turnaround has left him dull or short of his best, as a below-par front-runner who still leads could set a false or misleading pace.

Thursday Girl and Home Hero fighting for the lead — if neither concedes, watch the sectionals through the first quarter-mile; a genuine battle at the head of affairs for two furlongs or more will materially compress the chances of both leaders and inflate those of all prominent and hold-up profiles behind.

Tamzan is operating out of its natural hold-up position due to field congestion — if it finds itself in midfield traffic with no clear run into the straight, discount its finishing effort even if it appears well-placed at halfway.

Magic Trip returns from 77 days off — watch the market move in the hour before the race and the horse's behaviour pre-race; Andrew Balding's stable is in form but a long absence at this level means there is genuine uncertainty over peak fitness.

Glen Nevis with William Buick over a trip and going the horse handles well every time is a tactical pointer — if Buick slots in third or fourth early and is travelling smoothly at the three-furlong pole, that is a meaningful signal about the likely shape of the finish.

races.name: Killik Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Post Rider
runners_data.note: Oliver Cole's five-year-old is the lone confirmed pace-setter, giving Edmunds full control of tempo, but her recent form reads 73586 and she has not won in 15 similar-going starts — she sets the table more than she wins the meal, and her style-fit score reflects she may be operating at the limit of her natural role here.
runners_data.comment: Post Rider has run over today's trip and going before and steps in here with our rating of 76 suggesting she holds clear claims, but she remains winless in her last five starts and will need to find a sharp upturn in form to pose a serious threat.

runners_data.name: Box Clever
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's three-year-old brings course-form over this mile on Good ground — a win last time out at this trip and surface — and Jason Watson can slot in just behind Post Rider without burning energy, which is the most coveted position in this pace map; the seven-day turnaround is worth monitoring but Portman's 14-day record is solid.
runners_data.comment: Box Clever makes the perfect reappearance, winning last time out and returning fit just seven days later; she has run over today's distance and going before, and her rating of 80 marks her as the one to beat from stall one carrying 141 lb.

runners_data.name: Dark Rosa
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane partners a filly who by nature wants to race up with the pace, but with Post Rider and Box Clever already filling the prominent slots, she is likely to be squeezed back into a role that does not suit; her sim-going record on turf (0 wins, 2 places from 15) underlines that favourable conditions alone have not been enough.
runners_data.comment: Twice third in her last six starts and back in a quick 13 days, Dark Rosa has experience over today's trip and going and our rating of 80 makes her a leading threat at the weights; the risk is she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Kino Plasmat
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's lightly-raced three-year-old has run three times and finished fourth in all three, suggesting consistency without a winning breakthrough; Oisin Murphy takes the ride which is a significant booking, and a step up from seven furlongs to a flat mile on Good ground at Sandown looks a logical progression for a horse who has placed without threatening to lead on turf.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and rated 11 lb below her official mark on our figures, Kino Plasmat looks hard to fancy here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and 23 days since her last outing leaves her fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Poets Praise
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up type with Rossa Ryan in the plate — a potent combination if the pace scenario delivers a strong enough tempo for a late run; all three career runs have come at seven furlongs and this first mile test requires confirmation that the extra two furlongs suit, having been off for 42 days.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, Poets Praise nonetheless catches the eye with her rating of 74 suggesting she holds more ability than her official mark of 68 implies, and she has run over today's trip before; the risk is that her finishes have been modest and 42 days off the track adds an element of doubt.

runners_data.name: Perfect Ruler
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's gelding won over this mile on Tapeta last time, but all five turf starts have yielded placed efforts at best; he is naturally a prominent racer who is being squeezed out of position by the pace-rich configuration of this field, meaning Marco Ghiani will likely need to ride against the horse's instincts, which is a notable discount on his chance.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out — just 10 days ago — and has run over today's trip and going, with a trainer firing at 26% over the past fortnight; the weight of 133 lb is the main query, though her rating of 66 suggests she retains ability.

runners_data.name: Dandy Khan
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up type whose eight turf starts on similar going have produced only two placed efforts; Pat Cosgrave takes over at a short 8-day turnaround, and while his form figures of 565633 show a consistent mid-pack finisher, the compressed pace this shape is likely to generate does not obviously favour a horse that needs the race truly run.
runners_data.comment: Dandy Khan arrives in good nick just eight days after finishing third last time out, and a third two starts back shows consistent form, though she remains winless in recent starts and ranks sixth of eight on our rating.

runners_data.name: Pretty Spirited
runners_data.note: Lawrence Mullaney's filly has a genuinely strong profile on Good ground — two wins and three places from 13 such runs — and her natural running style is hold-up, though with more closers than the race shape can comfortably absorb she may find herself in a slightly more forward position than usual; Alec Voikhansky is a less prominent booking and the trainer's 14-day record is blank.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of eight on our figures, Pretty Spirited faces a stiff task despite returning in reasonable heart after a second last time out; she has run over today's trip and going before, though little in her recent form suggests she can trouble the leaders here.

races.paceDynamic: Post Rider is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Lewis Edmunds should be able to dictate a comfortable, controlled tempo over Sandown's flat mile without any rival applying pressure from the outside. That sustainable pace means the race is unlikely to truly test the stamina of those tracking, keeping the race shape compressed and the advantage with horses racing prominently or just off the leader rather than deep hold-up types waiting for a late injection of pace that may never arrive. The field does, however, contain more naturally prominent types than the map can accommodate: Box Clever is best placed to actually secure the position just off Post Rider, while Dark Rosa and Perfect Ruler — both genuine prominent racers — are likely to find themselves shuffled back and racing out of their preferred roles. This shape strongly favours a horse that can sit second or third, travel kindly on a fair pace, and produce a clean turn of foot from a handy position in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Post Rider sets an uncontested, even pace and Box Clever or another prominent type tracks comfortably before asserting in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Post Rider's solo front-running creates a genuinely fair tempo that rewards horses travelling prominently without burning fuel early, and the lack of a pace duel means the race turns into a test of quality from two out rather than raw stamina or a sprint finish from the rear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Pace Lift, Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If Post Rider's pace slows enough in the middle of the race to compress the field and release energy for true hold-up horses to pick up strongly entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo can occasionally compress the field to the point where genuine closers off the pace arrive with a sustained run, particularly if prominent horses use their energy racing wide or fighting for position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Pressured, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If Dark Rosa or Perfect Ruler push forward and challenge Post Rider for the lead, creating an untypically contested pace for this field.
scenarios.body: A contested early tempo would stretch the field and turn the race into a stamina examination rather than a quality sprint, benefiting the horse with the deepest reserves and the best finish over a truly-run mile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Burst, Surprise Result
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely approaching the final two furlongs and the race is decided by a single sprint effort from a mid-division position.
scenarios.body: A bunched, falsely-run race can produce chaotic results where a lower-rated horse finds a clear gap at exactly the right moment, and redistributed horses like Pretty Spirited or Perfect Ruler could benefit if they find themselves better placed than their mapped position suggests.

watchPoints.text: Box Clever's combination of a recent mile win on Good ground at this course and a prominent pitch just off Post Rider puts her in the perfect position if the pace is controlled — watch for Jason Watson taking a decisive grip approaching the two-furlong pole.

Dark Rosa and Perfect Ruler are both genuine front-runners who are likely to find themselves racing out of role and unable to get their natural position — if either pushes forward to challenge Post Rider, the tempo could spike unexpectedly and transform this into Scenario C.

Poets Praise has been off 42 days and all her starts have been over seven furlongs — she is stepping up in trip for the first time, and whether Rossa Ryan can deliver a held-up run over the extra distance on this pace shape is a key swing factor for the closers' scenarios.

Kino Plasmat's booking of Oisin Murphy for a horse with only three career runs is notable — Ed Walker tends not to call on Murphy unless the stable is confident, and a step to a flat mile on Good ground could see the horse's form improve sharply.

Pretty Spirited's Good-ground form is the strongest in the field statistically, but Alec Voikhansky's ability to execute a precise hold-up ride from a potentially more forward position than planned should be watched as a factor that could suppress her chance even if the horse is primed.

races.name: Killik Family Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Galyx
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the field and likely to lead unchallenged; her form at this trip and on Good ground is modest (sim-going: 0W0P in 5 runs) and she may find this a distance too far, but her positional role is irreplaceable in shaping this race — style fit is high for the job, not the result.
runners_data.comment: Galyx arrives in good nick on 17 days' rest, and his experience over today's trip and going is a solid foundation; our rating of 89 has him top-ranked of the nine, though he was only fourth two starts back and remains winless in recent starts, there is enough here to make him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Sharp Move
runners_data.note: Trained by William Haggas and ridden by William Buick — a top combination — this hold-up type drops back from 12f to 10f here having won at 10f on a synthetic surface; form is light on turf Good-ground evidence but class of connections is a standout factor.
runners_data.comment: Sharp Move won two starts back but has finished eighth on his most recent outing, and with a speed rating of 72 leaving him ranked seventh of nine on our figures, he looks to have plenty to find against stronger rivals here despite having run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Moon Angel
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer with two wins from four runs on Good ground at 12f, well-placed at OR=79 and back after 111 days; the layoff is a query but Stuart Williams has a respectable recent strike rate and this horse clearly loves conditions — 2W3P in sim-going is a strong profile for this shape.
runners_data.comment: Moon Angel showed a winner two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, but that 111-day absence is a notable query and her latest outing was a well-beaten eighth, leaving her with something to prove on return.

runners_data.name: Carnival Day
runners_data.note: Races prominently and has placed three times on Good ground, though without a win in 15 similar-conditions starts; Pat Cosgrave rides and the horse arrives on a tight turnaround (16 days), appearing solid rather than progressive under a rising handicapper profile at OR=75.
runners_data.comment: Carnival Day arrives here fit on a 16-day turnaround, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 85 puts him notably ahead of his official mark — a compelling angle for this gelding; yet to win in his last five starts, that winless run is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Sovereign View
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old hold-up horse stepping up significantly in trip from 8f to 10f, with all five recent runs on Tapeta; the single Good-ground run produced only a sixth and the switch to turf at this distance is a considerable unknown, though Rossa Ryan and James Tate merit respect.
runners_data.comment: Sovereign View has shown admirable consistency in recent starts, finishing in the first four on four of his last five outings, including third last time out, and our rating of 89 marks him as a genuine leading danger; the weight burden of 136 lb is the one factor to overcome.

runners_data.name: Golden Circet
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up specialist at OR=70 by profile, squeezed into midfield on the map because the field is rear-heavy — in reality Tom Queally will likely drop him in near the back; best form came over 16f (2nd) and dropping to 10f may blunt his stamina advantage, though he has placed twice in similar going.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Golden Circet's best recent effort was a third six starts back, though consecutive fourths two and three starts back suggest consistency without a breakthrough, and he faces a stiff task from draw 9 carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Magnatura
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced 3-year-old hold-up type wearing a visor, dropping back from 11f; showed a win at 7f and placed twice in 11-runner Good-ground fields, but has also finished 11th and 12th at this trip and beyond — inconsistency is the key concern for Sean Levey.
runners_data.comment: Magnatura showed up well with a third two starts back and has experience over today's trip and going, with our rating of 86 suggesting he merits respect; the concern is that he was unplaced last time out.

runners_data.name: Oh Yes You Do
runners_data.note: A true hold-up runner mapped to midfield due to the rear-heavy field composition — Billy Loughnane will likely drop him in at the back naturally; the horse has won twice and placed twice in Good-ground turf races and owns a solid record at 10f, making him interesting if the pace develops strongly enough to bring him into the race.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Oh Yes You Do is hard to fancy despite winning two of her last five starts, with a fifth on her most recent outing 48 days ago doing little to raise confidence; she has run over today's trip and going before, and stall three is her lot at 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Golden Phase
runners_data.note: Trained by Denis Coakley with Oisin Murphy taking the ride, which is a notable booking for a horse rated just OR=64; three wins from 15 similar-going runs shows a pattern of placing without dominating, but the prominent racing style and Murphy's positional intelligence give him relevance if the pace is modest.

races.paceDynamic: Galyx is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pace rival likely to contest that position hard, she should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 1m2f trip on Good ground at Sandown. Moon Angel, Carnival Day, and Golden Phase are all prominent types who will press forward behind Galyx, ensuring the race is not run at a crawl, but none looks likely to go head-to-head for the lead — meaning the pace should be honest without becoming injurious. The hold-up contingent — Sharp Move, Sovereign View, and Magnatura — will settle in behind a compact, orderly mid-to-rear group, and with Good ground allowing a true gallop, mid-to-late movers will need a strong sustained finish rather than a turn of acceleration off a slow pace. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace and outstay rivals in the final quarter-mile, as the tempo is unlikely to be either flat or chaotic. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear: Oh Yes You Do and Golden Circet are genuine closers who have been redistributed into midfield on the map, but in practice they are most likely to find themselves detached from the prominent group, making their task harder in a race where the pace is controlled rather than scorching.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Galyx Dictates, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Galyx leads uncontested and the prominent pack tracks her through a genuine but sustainable gallop.
scenarios.body: Galyx controls fractions from the front with Moon Angel, Carnival Day, and Golden Phase in close attendance, and the race is decided when those prominent horses kick from two out on the Sandown straight; horses racing handy into the final turn have the first run and the advantage in a race not run fast enough to fully bring the late closers into it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Turns Grind
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady enough that the race turns into a true stamina test in the straight, with hold-up horses staying on but unable to quicken past those already on the bridle.
scenarios.body: A modest-tempo lead from Galyx sets a rhythm that sees the race develop late, with the Sandown straight rewarding those who travel powerfully through the race and pick up from two out; horses carrying the highest OR and proven at the trip under Good ground gain the edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected — Moon Angel and Carnival Day both push forward early and drive the tempo higher — opening the door for closers.
scenarios.body: A genuinely-run race sees the prominent horses tire inside the final furlong, and the hold-up runners who have conserved energy sweep through late on the wide outside on Good ground; horses with high TS scores and strong closing sectionals are best suited.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Galyx eases the tempo dramatically and the field dawdles, producing a short, sharp sprint from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to take up the running and force the pace, the race becomes a bunch sprint off a slow early gallop, reducing it to a raw speed question over the last two furlongs; horses with the highest top-speed figures and a proven ability to quicken sharply are favoured.

watchPoints.text: Watch Moon Angel's starting freshness after a 111-day absence — if she bounces out smartly and settles behind Galyx with her ears pricked, she is set up perfectly for this race shape and her Good-ground trip form makes her the most dangerous prominent type.

Galyx carries a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 for racing out of role and her sim-going record (0W0P in 5) is poor — if she weakens turning in after leading, the prominent horses behind her will hit a wall of slowing traffic and those just off the pace will be better placed than those directly on her heels.

Oh Yes You Do and Golden Circet are true hold-up horses pushed into midfield by field composition — watch their early positioning; if both drop to the rear as expected, they will need the pace to be genuinely strong to have a realistic chance of getting involved in the final furlong.

Oisin Murphy taking the ride on Golden Phase (OR=64) is an eye-catching booking — monitor market movement; if Murphy is steering something with a live chance it typically shows up in the prices before the off.

Sovereign View has never run on turf Good ground beyond 8f — the step to 10f on a surface switch from Tapeta is a significant double-ask, and if he travels poorly early in the back-straight, Rossa Ryan may be forced to commit sooner than ideal for a hold-up type.
